name: Mount Vernon

dates.altered: The DHR entry: 'Through a series of alterations and remodelings, completed by 1787, Washington transformed a simple farmhouse built by his father into the mansion that it is today.'
dates.note: No single build date is stated by the sources read: the DHR gives 1754 as the date Washington became proprietor and 1787 as the completion of the remodellings; Wikipedia's categories place the house among '1757 establishments' and 'Houses completed in 1757'. The exemplar's year is the DHR's 1787 and says so.

ADDENDUM TO: MOUNT VERNON'), so no written data is quoted and this record carries no survey block.

note: Written 4 Sep 2026 from the WP-11.1 research pass; a new exemplar on georgian-colonial-american. HABS VA-505 carries photographs and no written data, so the archival references are what this record has. The new-england-georgian node's prose already names this house for its rusticated boards, which is a Northern trick on a Virginia house and the reason it stands for the parent rather than for tidewater-georgian.
